title: Unit 2: Differentiation: Definition and Fundamental Properties

topics.name: The derivative: definition and differentiability
covers: Defining the derivative of a function at a point and as a function

guide.title: Differentiation basics: review guide
guide.intro: The derivative measures an instantaneous rate of change: the slope of the tangent line. This unit covers its limit definition and the rules that make derivatives quick to find.

sections.title: Definition and differentiability
body: The derivative at a is the limit of difference quotients (average rates of change) as the interval shrinks. Notation: f′(x), dy/dx, or y′.
points: Differentiable at a point implies continuous there. The reverse is false: |x| is continuous at 0 but has a corner, so it is not differentiable.
A function is not differentiable at a corner, a cusp, a vertical tangent, or a discontinuity.
Tangent line at x = a: y = f(a) + f′(a)(x − a).

sections.title: Rules
body: Differentiate sums term by term and keep constant factors. Use the product and quotient rules for products and quotients. Do not just differentiate each part.

sections.title: Derivatives of elementary functions
body: Learn these by heart. They combine with the rules above.
points: Differentiate first, then substitute a value. Substituting first turns the expression into a constant, whose derivative is 0.

example.prompt: Find the tangent line to f(x) = x² + 3x at x = 1.
example.solution: f(1) = 4. f′(x) = 2x + 3, so f′(1) = 5. The tangent line is y = 4 + 5(x − 1), or y = 5x − 1.

misconceptions: A corner or cusp keeps a continuous function from being differentiable there.
“The derivative of a product is the product of the derivatives.”
“The order in the quotient rule doesn't matter.”
It does: the numerator is f′g − fg′, so swapping it flips the sign.

questions.explanation: Power rule: d/dx 3x⁴ = 3 · 4x³ = 12x³. The derivative of cos x is −sin x.
choiceExplanations: This lowers the exponent but drops the factor of 4 that comes down: 3 · 4x³ = 12x³.
The power rule lowers the exponent by one: x⁴ becomes 4x³, not 4x⁴.
The derivative of cos x is −sin x, not +sin x.

questions.prompt: f(x) = ln x. What is f′(4)?
choiceExplanations: ln 4 is f(4), the function value, not the derivative.
4 inverts the derivative. f′(x) = 1/x.
0 comes from substituting x = 4 first and then differentiating the constant ln 4. Differentiate first, then substitute.

questions.prompt: f(x) = x². Which expression equals f′(3)?
questions.explanation: By definition, f′(3) = lim h→0 [f(3 + h) − f(3)]/h, and f(3) = 9. This is the slope of a secant line as h shrinks to 0.
choiceExplanations: Without dividing by h this is the change in f, not a rate of change. It approaches 0.
The denominator should be x − 3 (the change in x), not x + 3.
This leaves out f(3). The difference quotient needs f(3 + h) − f(3).

questions.explanation: Product rule with f = x² and g = sin x: f′g + fg′ = 2x · sin x + x² · cos x.
choiceExplanations: This differentiates only sin x and leaves out the 2x sin x term.
This multiplies the two derivatives (2x times cos x). A product's derivative is not the product of the derivatives.
The product rule adds the two terms. Subtraction appears in the quotient rule.

choiceExplanations: This adds the two terms. The quotient rule subtracts.
This subtracts in the wrong order (x · 1 − (x + 1) · 1). The numerator is f′g − fg′.
1 comes from dividing the derivative of the top by the derivative of the bottom (1/1). That is not the quotient rule.

questions.prompt: f(x) = |x − 2|. Which is true at x = 2?
choices: f is continuous but not differentiable
f is differentiable but not continuous
f is both continuous and differentiable
f is neither continuous nor differentiable
questions.explanation: The graph has no break at x = 2 (f(2) = 0 and the limit is 0), so f is continuous. There is a corner: the slope is −1 on the left and +1 on the right, so f′(2) does not exist.
choiceExplanations: Differentiability implies continuity, so a function can never be differentiable but discontinuous.
The one-sided slopes are −1 and +1. They differ, so there is no single tangent line at x = 2.
f is continuous at 2. The graph is an unbroken V shape.

questions.prompt: What is the equation of the line tangent to f(x) = x³ − 3x at x = 2?
choiceExplanations: This swaps the slope (9) and the function value (2).
This uses f(2) = 2 as the y-intercept. The point (2, 2) is on the line, but not on the y-axis.
This subtracts f(2) instead of adding it: y = 9(x − 2) − 2.
